# NEO AI Research

> The public research corpus of the NEO AI Research Program. Every material
> statement carries a claim class: [E] established, with an external primary
> source; [A] architectural interpretation; [D] design intent, carrying a
> capability status; [O] open problem. Capability statuses resolve from a
> published register. Nothing in this corpus describes a deployed system
> unless its capability status says so.

## How to cite
Use the publication identifier and version, for example NEO-AI-P-007 v1.0, and
the permanent route https://neoai.myneogroup.com/id/NEO-AI-P-007


## Research papers
- [From Model Intelligence to System Intelligence: How Orchestration Compounds Capability](https://neoai.myneogroup.com/research/papers/model-intelligence-to-system-intelligence/): NEO-AI-R-009

## Institutional publications
None published yet.

None published yet.

## Method
- [How this corpus classes claims and reports capability](https://neoai.myneogroup.com/research/methodology/): claim classes, evidence tiers, how to cite, and what the Program will not claim

## Capability register
- [Capability Register](https://neoai.myneogroup.com/research/capability-register/): register version 1.3, Founder-ratified maturity classifications
- [capabilities.json](https://neoai.myneogroup.com/capabilities.json): machine readable

## Glossary
- [Controlled vocabulary](https://neoai.myneogroup.com/research/glossary/): one page per defined term

## Optional
Founder thesis and annotation: https://mickaelmosse.ai/

## What this file does not contain
No summary of any paper beyond its abstract, and no key-findings section. The Program publishes no benchmark and no comparison against any other system. A generated summary of a paper that reports no measurement is where an invented finding would come from, so none is generated.
